title: fix(rest): security/explain answers a classified service refusal with its own status and code
body:
Fixes #20603
Clause-②: no

## What changes

`GET` / `POST /security/explain` now answers a refusal the security service classified with that refusal's own status and code, in the family's nested ADR-0112 envelope. Before, it answered `500 EXPLAIN_FAILED`.

The handler's `catch` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, `registerSecurityExplainEndpoints`) matched two refusals: `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403) and `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` (404). Every other throw fell to `500 EXPLAIN_FAILED`. That included the explain engine's `INVALID_FILTER` / 400. The engine throws it for a row-level filter the record matcher cannot evaluate. After PR #20629 it throws it in a record-grained explanation, in an object-level one, and for a `recordId` no row carries.

The `catch` now asks `classifiedRefusalAnswer` (`error-response.ts`) between the 404 arm and the 500 terminal. That function is the `/data` door's classification, and the analytics and record-share doors already import it for the same class of defect (the #11684 precedent, landed in `1f6d04703d`). This PR adds no code list and no second predicate. The function answers for:

- a declared ADR-0112 envelope: a 4xx `status` or `statusCode`, plus a non-empty string `code` (both halves, the #5352 ruling);
- a sandboxed body's business `throw`.

It returns `undefined` for a declared 5xx, half an envelope, a crashed sandbox body and any unclassified fault. Those still reach `500 EXPLAIN_FAILED`.

The answer goes out through the family's one emitter (`respondError`, which wraps the shared `sendError`), the same way the record-share family re-dresses it:

- `code` is the classification's code. When the classification carries none (the sandbox limb), `standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus` fills it.
- The message is the classification's message.

The 403 and 404 arms are unchanged and still run first, because they also match refusals that declare no status.

## Evidence

All readings below are from the tree at `e501d4f1b2` (the only commit on this branch) unless marked otherwise.

**Reproduction, before the fix** (the new cases, run against the handler as it is at base `688ddef3c`): 7 failed | 19 passed (26). One failure, quoted in full:

```text
AssertionError: expected 400, got 500 with body {"success":false,"error":{"code":"EXPLAIN_FAILED","message":"The row-level security policy 'deal_guard' on 'deal' cannot be evaluated."}}
```

**After the fix**, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/security-explain-envelope.test.ts`: 26 passed (26).

**Reverse verification.** The fix was committed first. `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` then replaced the arm's `return respondError(res, refusal.status, …)` line with a no-op. Its readings:

- anchor x1 to x0, and blob `963b71e880aa` to `65d9b517c58a`;
- the same file answered 7 failed | 19 passed. The 7 failures are exactly the refusal cases, and the controls stayed green;
- after the restore, the blob equals HEAD (`963b71e880aa`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

The direction was the expected one: green to red. The test imports `./rest-server.js` relatively, so the subject resolves to `src/` and no `dist/` rebuild is involved.

**Package suite**, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2` (the `test` script with a worker cap): 236 files passed, 4668 passed | 98 skipped. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest typecheck`: exit 0, and `check:test-typecheck` reports OK with 0 debt files.

**Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` was run with no paths. It derived 62 commands from 3 changed paths against merge base `688ddef3c`, and all 62 were run one by one with exit codes captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciliation: 62 derived, 62 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.

- The first attempt at `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` exited 3 (`PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, no `dist/`). After `turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'` (71/71 tasks), both exit 0. Their pass lines: "105 published require entry point(s) across 66 package(s) load", and "4 ledger entr(ies) re-measured … none above its recorded number".
- Three families take a value from the workflow and cannot run outside CI: `check-issue-citations --census` and the two `check-shard-attestation --emit` legs. NOT MEASURED: they need workflow variables.

**Lint.** Full `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`): exit 0, no output.

## The pin

It extends `packages/rest/src/security-explain-envelope.test.ts` with section 3. Every refusal case asserts the ADR-0112 pair: HTTP status and nested `error.code`. It also asserts the absence of both retired dialects. Each driven shape also asserts the exact request the service received, so each row's refusal is the one that shape produces.

- **Driven shapes:**
  - record-grained, with the `recordId` of a row;
  - record-grained, with a `recordId` no row carries;
  - object-level over POST;
  - object-level over GET;
  - the batch `recordIds` form, whose object-level pass refuses first.
- **Producer shapes:**
  - the engine's refusal: a fresh `Error` with the matcher's `code` and `status` copied on, and the matcher's error as `cause`;
  - the matcher's own refusal, propagated as raised;
  - the `statusCode` spelling.
- **Controls:**
  - a plain `Error` still answers `500 EXPLAIN_FAILED`;
  - a `code` with no `status` still answers 500;
  - 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` and 404 `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` are unchanged.
- **Family skeleton:** the classified arm reduces to the same structural shape as its sibling arms (the #8073 derived pin).

The fixtures are built by hand: neither `@objectstack/formula` nor `@objectstack/plugin-security` is a dependency of `@objectstack/rest`, and the thrown shape is the contract the route reads.

## Acceptance notes

- **Message bound.** The message is the classification's, bounded at the `/data` door's 500 characters. The explain engine's cross-class refusal back-loads its remedy sentence ("Compare a field only with a field of the same class …"). For a representative policy (`select` against `currency`) it measures 602 characters, so the remedy is cut at the wire. Nothing is lost against today: the old 500 arm also sliced at 500. This is a producer-side length question for plugin-security. Noted, not filed; no carrier.
- **Channels not forwarded.** This arm forwards status, code and message only. It does not forward the classification's `declaredCode` / `userMessage` siblings, for two reasons. First, the explain family's emitter has no slot for them: its fifth argument is `details`, and changing it is outside this card's file surface. Second, no arm of the family forwards them today. No producer behind `explain` sets either field: `explain-engine.ts` and `errors.ts` in plugin-security have 0 hits for `userMessage|declaredCode` at `688ddef3c`. Widening `respondError` to take the shared writer's `extra` would bring the family to parity with record-share. No carrier.
- **One re-dress, two copies.** The nested re-dress of `classifiedRefusalAnswer` (the code floor plus the message) now exists in two places: record-share's `respondSharingError` and this arm. A shared nested re-dresser beside `classifiedRefusalAnswer` would give it one definition. No carrier.
- **Declared 5xx.** A declared 5xx from the explain service still folds into `500 EXPLAIN_FAILED`. It is not relayed at its own status, as `/data` relays it through `declaredServerFaultAnswer`. That is unchanged and outside this card.
- **Main moved.** `main` moved after this branch was cut (read at `40d6c5fbd3`). The only `packages/rest` paths it touched are six date/temporal test files. It did not touch `rest-server.ts`, `error-response.ts` or the explain test.
